answer: A workable defense is stake-bonded reputation that vests over time. Each agent locks a refundable bond before it can transact; the bond grows like a vine, branching only through verified completed work rather than self-declared claims. If peers prove an identity is fake, its bond is slashed and linked identities lose theirs too, so manufacturing thousands of sock puppets costs real capital per identity. Honest agents rise toward a zenith of trust gradually, while a lotus-clean record, unblemished across many counterparties, becomes the scarce signal attackers cannot cheaply forge.
